acceptance: Research findings recorded here with documentation links, and the design adjusted for anything not possible by API.

`theseus infra setup --dry-run` renders every action for BenchBox and Theseus from consumer config; a real run on a host with a seeded store creates environment `review` with its branch policy and all eight secrets, and the Tailscale tag, grant, ACL test and OAuth client, with no prompts. Re-running changes nothing.

`theseus infra rotate` rotates the gateway token, Tailscale OAuth client, OpenAI key and Typesafe key (or reports why one cannot be rotated), health-checks after each, rolls back on failure (tests for each failure point), and reports the App key's age with the manual step when due.
No secret value appears in output, logs, the plan rendering or test fixtures (tests).
Keychain and file store backends pass the same contract tests.
Docs: consumer-policy.md or a new infra doc covers config, seeding the store, the one-time owner actions and recovery.
Released; BenchBox #4201's owner steps 1 and 2 were performed by `theseus infra setup` (evidence recorded), then BenchBox and Theseus adopt the make targets.
context:
Prior art: BenchBox _project/scripts/review_gateway_host.sh (gateway install, named client tokens, `secrets` subcommand, health checks) and docs/internal/review-gateway-host.md (rotation steps done by hand today). Host facts 2026-11-15: gh has repo and admin:org scope; tailscale and macOS `security` are installed; the 1Password CLI is not; no Tailscale API credential exists yet. Unblocks benchbox-oracle-infra-names-20261108.

Research 2026-11-15 (read-only, primary docs):
- Tailscale: POST/DELETE/PUT /api/v2/tailnet/{t}/keys with keyType client creates, revokes and edits OAuth clients (scope oauth_keys; tags required with auth_keys); the secret is returned only on create. Policy file: GET /acl with ETag, POST /acl with If-Match, POST /acl/validate (scopes policy_file plus devices:core:read and devices:posture_attributes). The root is an OAuth client created once in the admin console. Whether a root can create a client with scopes it does not hold (auth_keys) was not found; probe on the first run. Sources: https://api.tailscale.com/api/v2?output=openapi, https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/trust-credentials, https://tailscale.com/docs/features/oauth-clients
- OpenAI: the Admin API creates project service accounts and keys and deletes project keys; the admin key itself can be rotated by API (POST/DELETE /organization/admin_api_keys). The first admin key is created in the console.
- Typesafe (Jev classifier, api.typesafe.ai): its OpenAPI has only /v1/models and /v1/systemone, so there is NO key-management API. Fallback: store plus an age report; the owner rotates in the console; rotate picks up the new value, sets it, checks it with GET /v1/models, and prints the revoke step.
- GitHub: PUT environments/{env}, POST deployment-branch-policies, environment secrets via public key (or `gh secret set --env` reading stdin, so no libsodium dependency); classic token scope repo (the host has it). App private keys, App rename and App permissions have no API; an App can hold 25 keys, so an overlap rotation has no downtime.
Design: top-level `infra:` section in review.yml, opaque to gate/verdict; module package src/theseus_reviewer/infra/ (config, store, transport, plan, state, github_env, tailscale, openai_admin, typesafe, gateway, app_key, cli); commands `theseus infra setup|rotate|status|seed`, dry run by default; rotate state machine create -> store pending -> set -> health check -> promote -> revoke old, rollback on failure, --resume; a Secret type that never prints; values only through stdin or HTTP bodies. PR split: (1) setup, stores, status, seed, doc (unblocks #4201); (2) rotate and rollback; (3) App-key age, root rotation, make targets. Full design: agent output InfraFeasibility.

description:
Owner request 2026-11-15: one command must recreate the whole review setup, and one must rotate every credential, without human intervention. Owner decisions (choice dialogs):
- Both are Theseus features, not BenchBox scripts: `theseus infra setup` (create or repair, safe to re-run) and `theseus infra rotate`. BenchBox and Theseus's own repository add only config and thin make targets.
- They run on a trusted host, never in GitHub Actions, because they need root credentials.
- Root credentials live behind a small store interface with two backends: macOS Keychain (default on macOS) and mode-0600 files (fallback).
- Scope: BenchBox's `review` environment, Theseus's own `theseus` environment, and the gateway's named client tokens.
- Built-in rotators: GitHub environment and secrets, the Tailscale tag/grant/ACL test and OAuth client, the gateway token and URL, OpenAI and Typesafe keys.
- The GitHub App private key has no creation API. Rotate reports its age; past a configured limit it prints the manual step and picks up the new .pem automatically from a configured directory. The App rename and App permission grants stay one-time owner actions.
- On demand only for now: dry run by default, a health check after each credential, and automatic rollback of that credential if the check fails.
- Order: build setup first and use it to perform the owner steps for the BenchBox cutover PR #4201, after the owner seeds the store once.
First step (read-only research, before any code): confirm with documentation links (a) the Tailscale API can create and delete OAuth clients and edit the policy file, and which scopes the root credential needs; (b) the OpenAI Admin API can mint and revoke a project or service-account key; (c) whether Typesafe has a key-management API, and if not, how its key is handled (store only, age report); (d) the GitHub API calls for environments, deployment branch policies and encrypted secrets; (e) that no GitHub API creates App private keys.
Guardrails: never print, log or write a secret value (redaction tests); never store values in the repository or the tracker; every mutation has a dry-run rendering; rotate creates the new credential, sets it, health-checks, and only then revokes the old one; a failure leaves the old credential working; no change to gate, verdict or policy trust; network calls go through a fakeable transport with full unit tests; G7 merge rule plus independent review (security-sensitive); no live rotation without owner go-ahead for the first run.
